name: St. Louis Lambert International Airport
before:
Missouri's largest and busiest airport, 14 miles north west of downtown St Louis, with nonstop flights to more than 80 destinations across the United States, Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean and Europe. It carried nearly 16 million passengers in 2024.

The terminal split is the thing to get right. Terminal 1 holds 36 gates across concourses A and C. Terminal 2 has 18 gates on concourse E, and every international flight without border preclearance is processed there. Moving between the two is by shuttle bus or on the Metro rail, which has been free between the terminals since July 2024.

MetroLink light rail also connects the airport to the rest of the metropolitan area, with a link to MidAmerica St Louis Airport 37 miles east planned.

Four runways serve the site, three parallel and one crosswind.

The airport is named after Albert Bond Lambert, the Olympic medallist and St Louis aviator, and made its name through Charles Lindbergh, its pioneering air traffic control and its years as the main hub for TWA.
after:
The main airport for St Louis, about 14 miles north west of downtown, handling more than 15 million passengers a year.

British Airways, the only UK airline with a direct service to St Louis, has flown here from London Heathrow since 19 April 2026, four times a week in the summer season.

The airport dates from 1920 and is named after Albert Bond Lambert, an early St Louis aviator. Charles Lindbergh flew the mail from here, and America's first air traffic controller worked here, directing aircraft with signal flags.
